scope: All six hosted pages; connected author screen; Account menu; source review of deposit, proving, validation, cancellation, recovery, moderation and withdrawal states.
coverage: Chrome live: boards.html, feed.html, user.html (fresh entry and the user’s successful-post state), fee-juice.html, censor.html, deploy.html, Account menu.
Code: shared controls/styles/error mapping; all six templates/controllers; relevant account, funding, claim, post and withdrawal operations.
Read-only audit: no payments, posts, moderation, withdrawals, wallet prompts or application modifications. Account menu restored closed; temporary viewport override reset.

Not live-exercised in this audit: failure injection, withdrawal settlement, moderator/deployer transactions, fresh-device passkey recovery, screen reader, light theme and true mobile viewport. Those findings are labelled Code; mobile remains an explicit verification gap.
principle: The interface should explain the user’s task and current state. Transaction accounting, bridge readiness and recovery belong to the application behind explicit interfaces.

findings.title: Posting is step 3 of a withdrawal wizard
findings.problem: A successful author sees “3 / 5” and a prominent “Proceed to Withdraw”. The product makes the main activity look incomplete.
findings.fix: End onboarding when posting becomes available. Make the board and composer the home screen; put “Get deposit back” in Account.

findings.title: Infrastructure copy precedes the actual task
findings.problem: Fee reservations, local proving data, privacy caveats and a vague alpha warning consume the first screen before Connect.
findings.fix: Lead with board identity, messages and one primary action. Show a short explicit testnet notice; put explanations at the decision they affect.

findings.title: The interface is a transaction log
findings.problem: Addresses, PXE, CRS, gas, raw timestamps, states and repeated confirmations are printed into the main interaction.
findings.fix: Render concise operation stages from application data. Put safe diagnostics in a collapsed Details panel with a copy action. Never parse logs to drive UI state.

findings.title: No consistent navigation or board identity
findings.problem: Reading, posting, fees, moderation and deployment feel like unrelated tools; the generic Billboard title does not identify the board.
findings.fix: Use a shared header with board name, Read, Write and Account. Keep operator tools in a separate area. Preserve verified board/network identity across links.

findings.title: Withdrawal warnings occupy the writing screen
findings.problem: Immediately after posting, the author is told that real posts need screening and sees a Censor Panel even without moderator rights.
findings.fix: Show posting readiness beside the composer. Show withdrawal preparation only when requesting the deposit back. Expose moderation rules as readable board information.

findings.title: There is no log out or switch account action
findings.problem: Account offers import/export tools but no normal way to leave the session; users are told to reload.
findings.fix: Add explicit Lock account and Switch wallet actions through the account API. Preserve pending-operation records and safely handle active work before switching.

findings.title: A returning user can be steered into a new passkey
findings.problem: Without browser metadata, Connect requests passkey creation, even if the person has an existing synced passkey. Import is hidden and requires Ethereum connection first.
findings.fix: Offer Use existing account and Create account at the right point in connection. Do not infer a new person from missing local storage.

findings.title: Connected and ready are conflated
findings.problem: A setup failure after account activation can leave Connect disabled and the manual wizard step without a Next or Retry setup action.
findings.fix: Separate wallet connection, private-account unlock and board readiness. Retry setup with the loaded wallet; preserve the meaningful failure.

findings.title: Recovery instructions point to a hard-to-reach screen
findings.problem: Recovery controls exist on setup. Back from posting opens deposit, which forwards a funded user straight back to posting.
findings.fix: Create persistent Activity access and contextual recovery actions on the affected operation. Remove navigation loops.

findings.title: Everyone is shown three technical recovery buttons
findings.problem: New users must distinguish Ethereum check/retry from Aztec recovery and understand nonce/proof language before doing anything.
findings.fix: Check relevant pending operations automatically. Present “Finish setting up”, “Check message” or “Check withdrawal” only when needed. Keep low-level tools in diagnostics.

findings.title: Passkey recovery and payment recovery are not the same
findings.problem: The passkey sounds sufficient, while claim secrets and pending requests may also require a recent encrypted backup. The caveat is buried in Account.
findings.fix: Make the recovery guarantee explicit and address missing payment recovery in the custody design. Offer an integrated backup flow when necessary; do not rely on remembering repeated manual exports.

findings.title: Account menu is a recovery-file form
findings.problem: Import passkey, import file, two password fields and export are all presented together. There is no useful account overview or distinct workflow.
findings.fix: Show wallet name/address, private-account status, balances and session controls first. Use separate Restore and Backup tasks with action-specific password fields.

findings.title: Backup validation becomes a generic failure
findings.problem: Password length and mismatch errors are replaced by a message about file, password, connection and an already loaded wallet.
findings.fix: Show the exact safe field error next to its input; distinguish wrong password, invalid file, account already open and storage failure.

findings.title: Current identity is separated from its controls
findings.problem: The full Ethereum address appears at the bottom while Account floats at the top; the private-account relationship is not clear.
findings.fix: Put a compact wallet label and shortened address in the semantic header, with full verified identities and copy actions inside Account.

findings.title: Deposit is not a comprehensible payment decision
findings.problem: The selected refundable ETH amount is prominent, but the action can first approve and fund a separate AZTEC balance. There is no numeric total-cost breakdown.
findings.fix: Before payment, show refundable deposit, AZTEC fee funding, estimated Ethereum gas and expected wallet confirmations. Distinguish funding credit from fees actually spent.

findings.title: The deposit slider lacks a concise decision summary
findings.problem: Minimum, maximum, cooldown, saved-up capacity and flagged-message penalties are spread across technical paragraphs.
findings.fix: Keep the requested slider. Present “Deposit X ETH · roughly one post every Y” and the actual board limits; explain burst allowance and penalties under Board rules.

findings.title: Funding and bridge waits look stalled
findings.problem: The useful state is hidden in logs; Processing does not say whether a wallet approval, network wait, proof or confirmation is pending.
findings.fix: Use named phases with completed steps, elapsed time, approval prompts and known waiting reasons. Use measured estimates only where supported; never fake percentages.

findings.title: Expected bridge delay becomes an error/retry task
findings.problem: After the bounded four-minute automatic availability wait expires, a pending message becomes an error telling the person to choose Resume setup later.
findings.fix: Keep the durable operation in a waiting state; continue safe readiness checks while open and resume after reopening. Offer a deliberate pause without re-sending the payment.

findings.title: Useful balances are missing from the main account view
findings.problem: The user cannot readily see refundable collateral, usable fee credit and actual spending; huge reservation numbers appear in logs instead.
findings.fix: Show these as three distinct concepts, with sensible precision and transaction details available on demand.

findings.title: The separate fee page retains manual bridge accounting
findings.problem: It exposes optional recovery-file and deposit-hash fields alongside a separate required Claim private balance step; success only tells the user to return.
findings.fix: Make Add transaction funds an integrated account task using the same funding coordinator and progress model, with credited balance on completion. Keep hash entry out of ordinary use.

findings.title: Fee controls are available without relevant state
findings.problem: Download recovery is always available and throws without a record; connecting enables Claim before a funding record necessarily exists.
findings.fix: Derive availability from actual funding state and show the reason where useful. Do not present impossible actions as valid choices.

findings.title: Fee amounts have machine precision and no useful recommendation
findings.problem: The live page says “65.7155471560548 AZTEC” and tells people to deposit more, exposing a reservation ceiling without a clear funding choice.
findings.fix: Show rounded readable amounts with exact values in details, a recommended top-up and its purpose. Do not imply a guaranteed number of posts from a variable network fee.

findings.title: Default remote proving lacks a visible explanation
findings.problem: Witness-sharing is mentioned only in a tooltip/ARIA description. “Post Anonymous Message” does not explain the additional trust in the prover operator.
findings.fix: Keep the single toggle. State visibly that private transaction information is shared with the configured prover operator, identify that operator, and provide fuller details accessibly.

findings.title: The proving toggle is visually broken
findings.problem: Global input styles give checkboxes full width, separating the checkbox from its label.
findings.fix: Use a compact, properly aligned checkbox or switch with a complete clickable label and normal keyboard behavior.

findings.title: Proving choice does not clearly communicate current work
findings.problem: The code correctly applies changes to the next operation, but that explanation is only a tooltip; a user can believe the running proof changed mode.
findings.fix: Keep operation configuration immutable. Show the active operation’s mode in its progress; make “applies to the next transaction” visible when relevant.

findings.title: Prover failures prescribe generic retries or reloads
findings.problem: “Try again or turn off Remote proving” does not distinguish offline, queueing, rejection or proof failure; reloading is a poor normal workflow.
findings.fix: Return safe typed service statuses through the API. Offer Retry or Use this device only when valid for the saved operation; never silently change trust modes.

findings.title: Ready is described as expiration
findings.problem: “Posting time lock has expired at the latest chain block” sounds like a failure. The waiting variant gives no actionable remaining time.
findings.fix: Use “Ready to post” or “You can post again in …”, driven by verified chain state. Do not claim readiness solely from a local clock.

findings.title: Screening is an unexplained author chore
findings.problem: Advance screening and “dummy post” expose protocol mechanics without saying what the action achieves, when it is needed or that it costs fees.
findings.fix: Remove it from normal composing. Orchestrate necessary screening inside an explicitly authorized withdrawal workflow, preserving moderation windows, verified eligibility and fee limits, and explaining fees and required approvals.

findings.title: Message validation can produce a wallet error
findings.problem: The 992-byte limit is checked only on submit; its uncoded error is replaced by a generic operation failure. Emoji and other scripts consume the limit differently.
findings.fix: Show a live capacity indicator and inline validation, preserve text, and prevent an invalid submission. Keep technical byte detail secondary.

findings.title: No explicit draft lifecycle
findings.problem: Text lives in the textarea and is cleared after success; there is no application draft model covering navigation, reload or account changes.
findings.fix: Define safe draft preservation scoped to board/account, with deliberate privacy/retention behavior. Preserve failed drafts and never silently publish a restored draft.

findings.title: Success is a pile of confirmations rather than a clear result
findings.problem: The live successful post shows duplicated Tx confirmed messages followed by fee and privacy lines in a scroll box.
findings.fix: Show one “Posted” confirmation, link/highlight the published message, and keep the composer available for the next post. Put fee/receipt detail under Activity.

findings.title: Public reading and logged-in reading are inconsistent
findings.problem: Different renderers, layouts, refresh behavior and older-message navigation make the same board feel like two products.
findings.fix: Share one feed presentation and navigation model while keeping public reading independent of wallet initialization.

findings.title: Messages lack ordinary context and stable sharing affordances
findings.problem: Cards show a sequence number and text, but no displayed publication time or individual share action.
findings.fix: Show readable time, a stable per-message link and status where relevant. Keep chain IDs and transaction hashes in details.

findings.title: The public reader omits the board rules
findings.problem: The writing screen shows moderation policy, while the read-only page does not render it. A reader cannot easily understand removals or posting rules.
findings.fix: Expose the same readable Board rules from both views, before someone pays to participate.

findings.title: New messages require manual refresh in the public reader
findings.problem: The public reader has no periodic refresh; older-history loading also asks the user to “Refresh to continue”, mixing two meanings.
findings.fix: Use an explicit new-message update affordance or gentle refresh that preserves reading position. Load history as history with bounded progress and a clear Older messages action.

findings.title: Reading status dominates useful content
findings.problem: “Messages loaded”, numbered cards, block progress and a self-link occupy attention; adjacent text links run together.
findings.fix: Use a compact navigation row, a proper Copy board link action and a quiet sync status only when useful. Give content the strongest hierarchy.

findings.title: Four indistinguishable boards are listed by address
findings.problem: The live directory exposes four existing boards as hexadecimal labels, without distinguishing the current board by purpose or freshness.
findings.fix: Add operator-provided names/descriptions tied to verified addresses, recent activity and availability. Identify the current test board and clearly mark retired operator deployments.

findings.title: Discovery makes the user operate a chain scan
findings.problem: Search complete through block … and Find more boards expose traversal mechanics without indicating useful progress or filtering.
findings.fix: Show usable results early, continue bounded discovery, and provide meaningful loading/empty/retry states. Keep scan position in diagnostics.

findings.title: Bad links and temporary outages share a useless retry
findings.problem: Invalid board/network links become “Could not load this board. Try again”, although retry cannot repair them.
findings.fix: Distinguish invalid link, unsupported network, unavailable board and temporary connection problems. Offer Browse boards or Retry as appropriate.

findings.title: Unavailable posting silently disappears
findings.problem: The reader hides Post a message when private fee settings are absent, without explaining whether the board is read-only or broken.
findings.fix: Keep a clear reading-only state and a short explanation of unavailable posting. Avoid showing a working board as an unexplained missing button.

findings.title: Withdrawal is exposed as two blockchain tasks
findings.problem: Withdraw ETH on L2 and Claim ETH on L1 require the user to understand notes, epochs, portals and bridge messages.
findings.fix: Present one Get deposit back journey with requested, waiting, ready for wallet confirmation and received states. Required wallet signatures remain explicit.

findings.title: Eligibility gives chores rather than a plan
findings.problem: Users are told to wait for real posts to mature and advance screening, with no clear count, readiness time or cost.
findings.fix: Show the refundable amount, why it is waiting, the next eligible time when known and any preparation/fee steps. Prepare through application APIs within the user’s authorized fee limits; preserve moderation windows and verify eligibility before each action.

findings.title: Normal settlement is presented as ERROR
findings.problem: Clicking Claim during expected network settlement produces BB_SETTLEMENT_PENDING through the error path.
findings.fix: Render an ordinary waiting state, check readiness automatically and only request the final Ethereum action when available. Persist progress across sessions.

findings.title: Final withdrawal has no completed screen
findings.problem: The final Claim button is re-enabled after success; clicking it again can generate an error because nothing remains to refund.
findings.fix: Show amount received, destination, receipt and Return to board. Derive available actions from completed state rather than restoring the old button blindly.

findings.title: Moderator navigation can change boards
findings.problem: Read, fund and older-message links omit the current board fragment, so destination pages can fall back to the hosted default board.
findings.fix: Generate every link from the verified current context and retain a return path. Add cross-board navigation tests.

findings.title: A moderator manually types a post number
findings.problem: There is no selected-message preview; parseInt can turn a decimal into another integer. A mistake can hide and penalize the wrong post.
findings.fix: Put Moderate on the actual message. Review the message, reason and concrete penalty before submission; validate integer identifiers strictly.

findings.title: Authority transfer has no clear consequence review
findings.problem: The form directly submits an address, with no recipient review or explanation that the current account loses control.
findings.fix: Use a dedicated transfer review with the full validated address, operator confirmation of the destination, and a loss-of-authority explanation before the final action.

findings.title: Immoral/censor/K language obscures board rules
findings.problem: The interface mixes censor, moderator and immoral, and displays K and time-lock arithmetic rather than the practical consequence.
findings.fix: Use Moderator and Hide for rule violation. Show the rule, reason and actual posting-delay effect; retain contract terminology only in diagnostics.

findings.title: Configuration overwhelms the moderator entry point
findings.problem: A raw JSON editor and infrastructure warnings precede the page title. The live empty page says settings are saved even when none is selected.
findings.fix: Lead with Select board and Unlock moderator account. Accept a board link/config file; put raw JSON and infrastructure settings behind Advanced. Correct empty/saved states.

findings.title: Policy editing lacks a clear review of what changes
findings.problem: An empty new-policy box and update action are separate from the current policy; local validation can become a generic wallet failure.
findings.fix: Edit from the current policy, show a change review and a live indicator of the actual UTF-8 byte limit, and provide precise field errors. Clearly state when the new rules apply.

findings.title: Board creation is a raw operator form
findings.problem: The page demands reviewed manifest files and optional gas JSON, then says “Be patient” about download size. It does not guide an operator to a usable board.
findings.fix: Separate Create board from advanced configuration. Show readable settings, validation and actual loading progress, with technical files available for operators who need them.

findings.title: Creation success does not reliably lead to a usable posting board
findings.problem: Omitting optional fee settings makes the exported file reading-only, while Use this board still routes to posting, which depends on separate hosted fee settings. Completion does not verify that hosted posting is available; pending deployment has vague resume instructions.
findings.fix: Use a deployment checklist with saved Resume state. Completion must show verified reading/posting/prover/moderator availability and route to what actually works.

findings.title: Safe validation errors are destroyed globally
findings.problem: The main status message for expected validation, message-length, cooldown and address errors can become a wallet/configuration/recovery failure. Some empty fields still receive useful inline feedback; that does not repair the misleading main status.
findings.fix: Use typed user-actionable errors with field/reason/action data through existing interfaces. Keep unexpected diagnostics sanitized without hiding the real next step.

findings.title: Status, cancellation, waiting and failure are conflated
findings.problem: Expected delays are red errors, successful readiness sounds expired, and broad instructions make the user diagnose several possible causes.
findings.fix: Define a consistent vocabulary: waiting for you, working, waiting for network, complete, cancelled and failed. Every actionable failure must offer the applicable action and say what was already completed.

findings.title: Important text has poor contrast
findings.problem: The live dark-mode policy is nearly invisible; fixed light-gray instruction colors are also unsuitable for light backgrounds.
findings.fix: Use explicit light/dark color tokens and verify contrast for text, links, warnings, disabled controls and focus states. Do not solve this by recoloring one sentence.

findings.title: Visual hierarchy makes routine actions look equally urgent
findings.problem: Purple recovery buttons dominate first-time entry, normal posting is secondary, and nested scroll boxes compete with the page.
findings.fix: Define primary/secondary/destructive actions consistently; use normal body typography for prose, generous reading rhythm, compact metadata and a single clear page flow.

findings.title: Visual and keyboard order do not agree
findings.problem: The fixed Account menu is appended at the end of the document; long technical logs are live regions, while changing posting readiness is not announced meaningfully.
findings.fix: Use a semantic header with matching DOM order. Announce concise phase changes, make diagnostics non-live, preserve focus and label actionable readiness updates.

findings.title: Motion and responsive behavior lack complete qualification
findings.problem: Animations have no reduced-motion override. The mobile viewport request in this audit still reported 755px, so true narrow-screen behavior was not verified.
findings.fix: Respect reduced motion and test real 390px layouts, zoom, keyboard and screen-reader flows. Check floating Account, long addresses, control wrapping and touch explanations.

findings.title: Loading and unavailable states expose the wrong affordances
findings.problem: Before initialization, Connect is absent but recovery buttons are visible and the remote toggle briefly appears off/disabled. The page looks half broken.
findings.fix: Render a coherent loading state with a meaningful status. Enable normal actions only when their prerequisites exist and show a useful Retry on failure.

findings.title: There is no concise support handoff
findings.problem: The interface offers generic recovery instructions and giant logs rather than a safe report for a specific failed operation.
findings.fix: Provide Copy diagnostic report containing safe operation ID, stage and error code, excluding keys, claim secrets and private witnesses. The app retains transaction accounting.
